children: Alphabet
delivered one of its strongest Google Cloud quarters yet, but the result was not enough to offset weaker advertising growth and another quarter of negative free cash flow.
Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to
$30.71 billion
in the third quarter, beating Wall Street expectations as enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and cloud services remained strong.
The cloud business is becoming increasingly important to Alphabet's AI story.

Google said sales of its custom tensor processing units, or TPUs, have become a meaningful contributor to Cloud revenue. The company only recently began recognizing revenue from direct sales of complete TPU systems, including chips, hardware and software.
Demand visibility also remains substantial.
Google Cloud's backlog reached
$561 billion
, with Alphabet expecting to recognize more than 55% of that amount as revenue over the next 24 months.
The problem is what it costs to support that growth.
Alphabet generated
negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion
during the quarter, marking its second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Management also expects 2027 capital spending to rise significantly from the company's 2026 forecast of
$195 billion to $205 billion
That spending pressure overshadowed the cloud beat.
Alphabet reported total third-quarter revenue of
$127.6 billion
, below the $128.2 billion consensus estimate, while advertising revenue of $82 billion missed expectations of $83.4 billion. Shares fell about
10% after hours
Search also became a bigger concern.
Management attributed some of the slowdown in search advertising growth to increased use of AI Mode, where Google is still experimenting with ad monetization.
Investor Takeaway
I think Alphabet's quarter creates a very clear tension.
Google Cloud is proving that AI demand is real. The question is whether the returns on that demand will justify the spending required to serve it.
The cloud numbers are hard to dismiss. Revenue more than doubled, backlog reached $561 billion, and TPUs are becoming a more meaningful commercial business.
But Alphabet is also burning cash at a rate that investors are not used to seeing from Google.
That shifts the debate away from whether Alphabet can compete in AI and toward whether AI can become sufficiently profitable to offset the enormous infrastructure bill.
For investors, the key things to watch are
Google Cloud growth, TPU sales, search monetization inside AI Mode, free cash flow, and 2027 capex guidance
Cloud is carrying the AI story.
Now Alphabet has to prove the economics can carry it too.

title: Alphabet's Cloud Surge Comes With a Massive Catch
